eligibility_reason: This paper reports original quantitative content-level estimates from a defined sample of 100 most-liked English-language TikTok videos about sunscreen. It explicitly classifies 6% of the videos as inaccurate according to American Academy of Dermatology sunscreen guidelines.

estimates.denominator: the 100 most-liked TikTok videos about sunscreen in the sample
estimates.measure: share of sampled videos classified as inaccurate
estimates.misinfo_definition: Inaccurate content classified according to concordance with the American Academy of Dermatology sunscreen guidelines
estimates.source_quote: Out of the 100 videos, 35 (35%) were classified as accurate, 6 (6%) as inaccurate, 2 (2%) as mixed, and 57 (57%) were opinion-based or not applicable for factual accuracy evaluation.

considered_but_excluded.why: Positive attitude toward sunscreen, not misinformation prevalence.
Videos classified as accurate; this is not prevalence of misinformation.
Videos classified as mixed accuracy; the paper does not define this category as misinformation or quantify its misinformation share separately.
Opinion-based or not applicable for factual accuracy evaluation; not equivalent to misinformation prevalence.
Global Quality Score categories, measuring content quality rather than misinformation prevalence.
Promotional content, an adjacent construct rather than misinformation prevalence.
Creators identifying as health care professionals, a creator characteristic rather than misinformation prevalence.
Videos containing sunscreen product recommendations, not misinformation prevalence.
Videos receiving poor or below-average quality scores, measuring quality rather than misinformation prevalence.
